producer_report.summary: Added crates/athena-core/src/learning.rs with `join`. It gives one line per repeated failure class: the class, the addressing request with its landed or open state, and the outcome of that request's class of work (specialization verdict and minutes trend). `Records::status` fills a new `StatusView.learning` field. `display.rs` prints the lines under the `repeated` label and prints nothing when no cause repeated. OLY-9-09 in docs/spec.toml now names the mechanism and a measure ending in `status: repeated`. CHANGELOG.md is updated.

checks_run.note: One timing-sensitive drain test (a_group_of_urgent_items_does_not_start_ahead_of_the_improvement_turn) failed in the full parallel run and passed when rerun alone. Everything else passed, including the unit tests in display.rs and the xtask spec and policy tests.

criteria_check.criterion: docs/spec.toml OLY-9-09 has mechanism naming the new crates/athena-core module and its function (not "none"), owner "Athena", and a measure ending in `status: repeated`.
criteria_check.evidence: docs/spec.toml OLY-9-09 mechanism is "crates/athena-core/src/learning.rs (join, ...)", owner is "Athena", and the measure ends in `status: repeated`. The xtask tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core learning`: a fixture with a repeated failure class, a landed addressing request, and a specialization/class-trend outcome yields one line per class that names the class, the request and its landed/open state, and the outcome. The same test fails if the join function is stubbed to return nothing.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core learning`: 2 tests pass. The first asserts the exact lines for two classes and that a cause with no class is left out. A stub that returns nothing would fail its `lines.len() == 2` and line assertions. I did not run a stubbed version.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: the status display prints the new lines under the `repeated` label, and prints nothing extra when there are no repeated causes (an empty history is not shown as success).
criteria_check.evidence: The display.rs test asserts `learning_section(&[], true) == ""`, the line under the `repeated` label, and an indented line when an open cause already printed the label. `cargo test -p athena-cli` passed except one timing-sensitive drain test, which passed on rerun.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test` for the workspace, including the xtask spec test that checks the measure marker; it passes.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-cli -p xtask`; both pass apart from the one drain test noted above, which passed alone. I did not run the whole workspace in one command.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`; both are clean.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all`, which applied formatting.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff changes only docs/spec.toml and files under crates/ (the new module, its mod line in lib.rs, status.rs and display.rs wiring), and adds no secrets or personal data.
criteria_check.evidence: The changed files are the new learning.rs, lib.rs, status.rs, display.rs, docs/spec.toml, and CHANGELOG.md, which the brief lists as a deliverable. No secrets or banned words were written.

open_issues: The drain test parallel::a_group_of_urgent_items_does_not_start_ahead_of_the_improvement_turn failed once in the parallel run and passed alone. It looks timing-dependent and unrelated to this change.

I did not run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on its own. The policy test ran as part of `cargo test -p xtask` and passed, but it reads only tracked files, so it did not scan the new learning.rs. I reread that file against the banned words and found none.
learnings: Records::status only keeps open repeated causes in StatusView.repeated_causes. The learning join therefore uses the unfiltered repeated_causes so that landed requests show.
RepeatedCause.class is a registry failure class, not a class of work. The outcome comes from the addressing request job's class of work (JobRecords::class).
